caption:
Midjourney and Google's Nano Banana are the two image AIs most people end up choosing between.
Midjourney V8.2 is built for striking, styled images and starts at $10 a month. Nano Banana 2 lives in the free Gemini app and is best at editing your own photos.
Here is which one fits what you want to make.

Which one do you use for AI images?

threads_text: Midjourney has no free trial on its website and starts at $10 a month. Nano Banana 2 is free in the Gemini app and edits your own photos from a plain sentence. Would you pay for Midjourney if the free option is good enough?

slides.headline: *Midjourney vs Nano Banana*: which image AI to use, and what each one costs

slides.heading: 1. Midjourney is on *V8.2*
paras: Midjourney V8.2 has been the default model since July 24, 2026. It aims for bolder, more original images.
Each prompt returns four images. V8.1 added 2K output in HD mode and renders 4 to 5 times faster.

image.credit: Midjourney V8 image prompted by The Decoder

slides.heading: 2. Nano Banana is *free* in Gemini
paras: Nano Banana 2 makes and edits images inside the Gemini app, with no paid plan needed.
Paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana 2.1, higher limits and a Redo with Pro button.

slides.heading: 3. Midjourney has *no free tier*
paras: Midjourney plans start at $10 a month. There is no free trial on its website or in Discord.
Unlimited images in Relax mode start with the Standard plan at $30 a month.

slides.heading: 4. Editing *your own photos*
paras: In Gemini you upload a photo and describe the change in plain words. It can even translate a sign.
Midjourney's Edit Model takes up to four of your images on V8.1 and V8.2.

site_article.headline: Midjourney vs Nano Banana: which image AI to use, with plans and limits compared
site_article.dek: Midjourney V8.2 is a paid tool built for striking, styled images. Nano Banana 2 is free inside the Gemini app and strongest at editing photos you already have. Here is how to pick.
site_article.summary: Midjourney's default model is V8.2 and its plans run from $10 to $120 a month, with no free trial on the website. Google's Nano Banana 2 is free in the Gemini app, and paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana 2.1 and Nano Banana Pro.
site_article.seo_title: Midjourney vs Nano Banana: which AI image tool to use
site_article.seo_description: Midjourney vs Nano Banana compared: current models, free access, plan prices, limits, photo editing and text in images, plus prompts to test both side by side.
site_article.answer_summary: Pick Midjourney if you want the most striking, styled images and are willing to pay at least $10 a month. Pick Nano Banana if you want a free tool that edits your own photos from a plain sentence and handles text inside images.
site_article.hero_alt: Google promotional image with the words Nano Banana 2 surrounded by AI generated pictures.

paragraphs.text: Midjourney vs Nano Banana is the choice most people face when they want AI images that look good. Midjourney is an independent image lab, and its default model has been V8.2 since July 24, 2026. Nano Banana is the nickname for Google's image models inside the Gemini app. The free one is Nano Banana 2, which Google launched on February 26, 2026, and paid Google AI plans now also get Nano Banana 2.1.

The short answer: Midjourney is the better pick when the look of the picture matters most and you are happy to pay for it. Nano Banana is the better pick when you want to change a photo you already have, put readable text in an image, or simply not pay anything.
Midjourney vs Nano Banana at a glance

Current models: Midjourney says V8.1 replaced V7 as its default after user testing, and V8.2 followed with a focus on images that are more inventive, refined and original, fewer random low quality results, and personalization that understands your taste better. On Google's side, the Gemini app uses Nano Banana 2 with the Flash and Pro models and Nano Banana 2 Lite with Flash-Lite. Decrypt reported that Nano Banana 2.1 began rolling out on October 6, 2026.

How you work: in Midjourney you type a prompt and get a set of four images to choose from. In Gemini you chat. You ask for an image in a normal sentence, then reply with changes, and Google's help page shows how to open a picture from your Library and keep editing it in the same chat.

Image size: Midjourney says V8.1 in HD mode generates 2K images without upscaling, and that standard jobs render about 4 to 5 times faster than earlier versions. Google says Nano Banana 2 supports resolutions from 512 pixels up to 4K. In the Gemini app, the help center says full size downloads are 2K with a Google AI plan and 1K without one.

Text and real things: Google says Nano Banana 2 can render legible text, translate the text inside an image, keep up to five characters looking the same and keep up to 14 objects consistent in one workflow. It also draws on web search to get specific real subjects right. Midjourney says V8.1 renders text better than any of its earlier models.
Free access and prices

Midjourney is paid. Its Free Trials page says no free trial is currently available on Discord or the midjourney.com website, only a limited trial in the niji journey app for iOS and Android. Plans cost $10 a month for Basic, $30 for Standard, $60 for Pro and $120 for Mega, or $8, $24, $48 and $96 a month when billed yearly.

What the plans give you: Basic includes 3.3 hours of Fast GPU time a month and no Relax mode. Standard has 15 hours plus unlimited images in Relax mode. Pro has 30 hours and adds Stealth mode, which Basic and Standard lack. Mega has 60 hours. Midjourney says a company with more than $1 million in yearly gross revenue must buy Pro or Mega.

Nano Banana 2 is free in the Gemini app. Google's plan comparison lists image generation with Nano Banana 2 for every user, including people without a plan, while Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers can also redo an image with Nano Banana Pro. Google's Nano Banana page says Nano Banana 2.1 needs a Google AI plan and that paid plans get higher generation limits.

Gemini's limits are not a fixed number of images. Google's help center says usage refreshes every 5 hours until you reach a weekly limit, that image requests use more of it than text, and that AI Plus gets 2 times the standard limits and AI Pro 4 times. If you run out of your daily Nano Banana 2 images, you also cannot redo more images with Nano Banana Pro.

For most people the price decides it. Nano Banana costs nothing to try, so start there. Midjourney makes sense once you know you want its style every week, and the $30 Standard plan is the first one where you stop watching the clock, because Relax mode images are unlimited.
Which one to pick

paragraphs.title: 1. You want to fix or change a photo you took
paragraphs.text: Use Nano Banana in Gemini. Upload the photo, say what to change in one sentence, and reply with corrections. Google's help page says editing images requires you to be 18 or older on a personal account.

paragraphs.title: 2. You want a striking image from nothing
paragraphs.text: Use Midjourney. V8.2 is tuned for bold, original looks, and personalization profiles learn your taste from the images you rate.

paragraphs.title: 3. You need words inside the picture
paragraphs.text: Start with Nano Banana. Google lists legible text, translation and infographics among its strengths, and Nano Banana 2.1 on paid plans adds better world knowledge for diagrams.

paragraphs.title: 4. You want precise edits inside Midjourney
paragraphs.text: Use the Editor on the Midjourney website. You can erase an area and regenerate it, move or resize the image on the canvas, or retexture the whole picture in a new style while keeping its layout. The Edit Model also takes up to four of your own images on V8.1 and V8.2.
Prompts to test both side by side

Run the same prompt in both tools before you decide. Keep it short and concrete: one subject, one place, one kind of light. Then compare the first results, not the best of ten tries, because that is what your credits or free limit will buy you.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A product shot
paragraphs.text: A ceramic coffee mug on a wooden kitchen table, soft morning light from a window on the left, steam rising, shallow depth of field

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Text in the image
paragraphs.text: A hand painted wooden sign outside a small bakery that says "Fresh Bread Daily" in white letters, street photo, late afternoon

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Edit your own photo (Gemini)
paragraphs.text: Change the background of this photo to [place], keep my face, clothes and pose exactly the same, and match the light to the new scene.
Where each one falls short

Midjourney's newest models drop some older tools. Its docs list features that V8.1 does not support, including Character Reference, Omni Reference, Draft Mode, Turbo Mode and the Quality parameter. Maverick Frame reported that Midjourney said on November 11, 2026 it is aiming to ship V9 within 30 days, which could change how style references and personalization behave.

Gemini marks every image as AI made. Google says images from the Gemini app carry an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible watermark. Google also says limits can change without notice, including when capacity is tight.

The honest trade is control against cost. Midjourney gives you more ways to steer a style, but every image spends paid GPU time. Nano Banana is free and quick for everyday edits, yet the visible watermark and shifting limits make it a weaker fit for client work. Quality claims on both sides come from the companies, so ten minutes with your own prompt tells you more than any spec sheet.
